'''Laura Mersini-Houghton''' (''née'' '''Mersini''') (born around 1970) is an Albanian-American [[cosmologist]] and [[theoretical physicist]], and professor at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. She is a proponent of the [[multiverse]] hypothesis and the author of a theory for the origin of the universe that holds that our universe is one of many selected by quantum gravitational dynamics of matter and energy.  Mersini-Houghton has claimed that her theory explains unusual astrophysical data.<ref name="TG-20220827">{{cite news |last=Fox |first=Killian |title=Cosmologist Laura Mersini-Houghton: 'Our universe ==Biography==
Laura Mersini was born in [[Tirana]], Albania, as a daughter of the mathematician and eminent economist Nexhat Mersini.<ref name="dedaj">Dedaj, Valeria (16 September 2015). Big Bang-u dhe sfidat e shkencetares shqiptare  (Big Bang and the challenges of Albanian scientists), in Albanian. Retrieved from https://www.shqiperia.com/Big-Bang-u-dhe-sfidat-e-shkencetares-shqiptare.30485/.</ref><ref name="peshku">Peshku pa ujë (19 July 2012). Laura Nexhat Mersini, vlonjatja shkencetare. Retrieved from http://arkivi.peshkupauje.com/2012/07/laura-nexhat-mersini-vlonjatja-shkencetare {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180211071711/http://arkivi.peshkupauje.com/2012/07/laura-nexhat-mersini-vlonjatja-shkencetare |date=11 February 2018 }}.</ref>

Mersini-Houghton received{{when|date=January 2017}} her B.S. degree from the [[University of Tirana]], [[Albania]].{{citation needed|date=January 2017}}

In 1994, Mersini-Houghton was a Fulbright scholar at the University of Maryland, College Park for 8 months.<ref name = "UNC">[http://physics.unc.edu/people/mersini-houghton-laura/  University of North Carolina, Department of Physics and Astronomy]</ref><ref name = "BalkanWeb">[http://www.balkanweb.com/site/shkencetarja-shqiptare-pas-aprovimit-te-teorise-per-universin-pretendente-per-nobel/ Balkanweb, Shkencëtarja shqiptare pas aprovimit të teorisë për universin, pretendente për"Nobel"]</ref>

In 1997, Mersini-Houghton was awarded her M.Sc. by the [[University of Maryland]].<ref name = "UNC"/>

In 2000, Mersini-Houghton completed her Ph.D. at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]].<ref name = "UNC"/>

From 2000 to 2002, after earning her doctorate, Mersini-Houghton was a postdoctoral fellow at the Italian [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]].<ref name = "UNC"/>

From 2002 to 2003, Mersini-Houghton had a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Syracuse University]].<ref name = "UNC"/>

In January 2004, Mersini-Houghton accepted a position as assistant professor of theoretical physics and cosmology at the [[University of North Carolina]]. In a series of papers published between 2004 and 2006, she presented a theory that the universe arose from a multiverse, and made a series of testable predictions which included the existence of the [[Giant Void]]. She was granted tenure in 2008 and promotion to associate professor in 2009 and full professor later.<ref name = "UNC"/>

On 11 October 2010, Mersini-Houghton appeared in a BBC programme entitled ''What Happened Before the Big Bang'' (along with [[Michio Kaku]], [[Neil Turok]], [[Andrei Linde]], [[Roger Penrose]], [[Lee Smolin]], and other physicists), where she propounded her theory of the universe as a wave function on the landscape multiverse.<ref name="BigBang">{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00vdkmj |title=Two Programmes - Horizon, 2010-2011, What Happened Before the Big Bang? |publisher=[[BBC]] |date= |accessdate=2 January 2011}}</ref> Mersini-Houghton's work on multiverse theory is discussed in the epilogue of a recently published biography of [[Hugh Everett III]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Byrne|first1=Peter|title=The many worlds of Hugh Everett III : multiple universes, mutual assured destruction, and the meltdown of a nuclear family|date=2010|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford|isbn=978-0-19-955227-6|edition=1st}}</ref> Her predictions were successfully tested recently by the Planck satellite experiment. See also a discussion of her ideas in the context of the history and philosophical implications of the idea of a multiverse here.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Rubenstein|first1=Mary-Jane|title=Worlds Without End: The Many Lives of the Multiverse|date=2014|publisher=[[Columbia University Press]]|location=New York|isbn=978-0-231-15662-2|edition=1st}}</ref>

In September 2014, Mersini-Houghton claimed to demonstrate mathematically that, given certain assumptions about [[Firewall (physics)|black hole firewalls]], current theories of black hole formation are flawed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://briankoberlein.com/blog/yes-virginia/|author=Brian Koberlein|date=25 September 2014|title=Yes, Virginia, There Are Black Holes|website=One Universe at a Time|accessdate=17 October 2014}}</ref>  She claimed that [[Hawking radiation]] causes the star to shed mass at a rate such that it no longer has the density sufficient to create a black hole. With Stephen Hawking, she organized a historic conference in 2015 in Stockholm to discuss these fundamental topics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uncnewsarchive.unc.edu/2014/09/23/carolinas-laura-mersini-houghton-shows-black-holes-exist/|title=Carolina's Laura Mersini-Houghton shows that black holes do not exist|accessdate=22 August 2022|date=23 September 2014|publisher=[[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]}}</ref><ref name="wncn">{{cite web|url=http://www.wncn.com/story/26606303/unc-professor-says-black-holes-cant-exist|title=UNC professor says black holes can't exist|accessdate=24 September 2014|date=23 September 2014|publisher=WNCN|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021024434/http://www.wncn.com/story/26606303/unc-professor-says-black-holes-cant-exist|archivedate=21 October 2014}}</ref>

==Teaching==
Mersini-Houghton teaches graduate and undergraduate classes in Quantum Mechanics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. https://physics.unc.edu/people/mersini-houghton-laura/
